title: How to run a fundraising process: Jason Calacanis' investor funnel, pitch rules and follow-up playbook
summary: Jason walks through items 81-90 of his startup checklist: pitch rules, building a curated list of about 150 investors, a short cold email with a Loom, nailing the first meeting, following up, backdoor-referencing investors, and SEC basics. He treats fundraising as a sales funnel, a numbers game where careful targeting and practice matter most.

principles.text: Curate a targeted list of ~150 investors, matched by firm, partner, and stage, then follow up two or three times.
principles.quote: you want to make a qualified list of targets we suggest 150 in the launch accelerator 150 people you email them you follow up with them two or three times

principles.text: Treat fundraising as a sales funnel: many targets narrow to only a few term sheets.
principles.quote: 150 targets really carefully selected to get but one two three four term sheets

principles.text: Make the cold email a short trailer, not the whole movie, with a quick demo or Loom to earn the meeting.
principles.quote: the trailer is not the entire movie the trailer is to get you to buy a ticket to the movie that's what this email is

principles.text: Every custom Loom is another rep; send many, learn from replies, and lead with your strongest asset.
principles.quote: every time you do one of these looms it's another rep it's you getting another swing at bat

principles.text: Practice on lower-priority investors first, then pitch your dream investors in weeks two or three.
principles.quote: start with the people you're not really concerned with winning them as a business and then you know the people you really want to win as investors and partners you can put in week two or three

principles.text: Answer investor questions concisely, like ping pong, and end every meeting with clear next steps.
principles.quote: you answer the question in as much time as they took to ask the question that's ideal
